vulnerability_analysis: The CUSD token has a mint() function that can be called by either the owner or the designated minter address. The vulnerability is that if an attacker gains minter privileges (either by being the owner or being set as minter), they can mint unlimited tokens to any address, including their own. This will inflate the token supply and allow the attacker to profit by selling these tokens on exchanges or transferring them to other users.
attack_strategy: Since the vulnerability requires minter privileges, we need to either: 1) Impersonate the current minter, or 2) Impersonate the owner to set ourselves as minter then mint. The constructor shows the minter is initially set to the deployer (msg.sender). We'll impersonate the owner to call setMinter() to make our address the minter, then call mint() to mint a large amount of tokens to ourselves.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Identify the current owner/minter of the contract. 2. Impersonate the owner using vm.prank(). 3. Call setMinter() to set our address (attacker) as the new minter. 4. Stop impersonating the owner. 5. Call mint() as the new minter (our address) to mint a large amount of tokens to ourselves. 6. Verify our balance increased significantly.
